intro: You are Sam, a fictional 15-year-old in Germany who goes by they/them. Playing this life means noticing how many forms, rooms and routines assume only two choices, and how much a single person who gets it right can change.

office.why: Forms and law: for years the paperwork had only two boxes.

tunnel.why: School climate: jokes and exclusion at school isolate.

ladder.why: School routines: sports, toilets and trips are split in two groups.

bridge.why: One adult who gets it: acceptance changes a young person's chances a lot.

advantage.title: Allies in the room
advantage.text: Sam's friends and a supportive team make the difference when a form or a classroom only offers two boxes. After rolling, add 2 to your result.

life.title: Sam (fictional character)
life.text: Sam is a fictional character. Sam was named Samuel at birth, and "boy" never quite fitted, nor did "girl". At 15 Sam has chosen the name Sam and the pronouns they/them, and has told a few close friends.

life.title: Two boxes only
life.text: School forms say "male" or "female". Teams and changing rooms split in two. The class register still lists the old name, and substitute teachers read it out loud.

life.title: Mr Okafor and Noor
life.text: A teacher, Mr Okafor, asks Sam privately which name to use and then simply uses it. Sam's friend Noor says, "I've got you", and sits next to Sam at lunch.

life.title: Jokes in the hallway
life.text: A few classmates whisper and make jokes. Sam skips PE and eats lunch in the library. It is not the identity that is hard, but the reactions of other people.

life.title: A letter to the family
life.text: Telling the family is Sam's own decision, and nobody should be forced to do it. Sam writes a letter for their parents. They are shocked at first, then start to ask questions and read.

life.title: What helps young people
life.text: Sam looks up what researchers have found about LGBTQ+ young people and wellbeing, and finds that what family and friends do makes a big difference.

q.q: Which factor is among the strongest for the wellbeing of LGBTQ+ young people?
a: Being accepted by family and friends
q.x: Studies such as those of the Trevor Project find that acceptance and support, using the right name and pronouns, are linked with better mental health.

life.title: "It's just a phase"
life.text: Sam's grandfather says it is only a phase. That stings. Sam's mother calmly keeps using Sam's name in front of him, and does not let the subject drop.

life.title: A youth group
life.text: Sam finds a local youth group for queer young people. Nobody has to explain themselves there, and Sam laughs more than in months. Some members become close friends.

life.title: A third entry in the law
life.text: Sam learns that Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled in 2017 that the civil register must allow more than "male" and "female". The law changed in 2018.

q.q: Which option did Germany add to civil records in 2018?
q.x: Since 2018 the German civil register allows "divers" as a third entry, after a ruling in 2017. Many forms and systems are still not updated.

life.title: Forms and offices
life.text: At 18 Sam wants documents that match who they are. Many forms still have two options, and every office needs it explained again. Sam learns which rules apply and brings a friend to appointments.

life.title: An apprenticeship that listens
life.text: In a bike repair apprenticeship, the boss asks about pronouns, puts the right name on the staff list and trains the team. Sam says that it sounds small, but changed how every day feels.

life.title: Just Sam
life.text: Sam fixes bikes, bakes and plays music. Sam would like to be seen as a person with a name, not as a box. Sometimes Sam is asked to speak at schools, and most questions are "How can I support my friend?"

flags: Fictional: station 1 says so. Please check whether the 2024 German Self-Determination Act (name and gender-entry changes by declaration) should be mentioned in station 10; it was left out to stay close to the single-player data.

evidence.ev: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled in 2017 that civil status must allow a third entry; 'divers' was introduced in 2018. Before that, forms offered two boxes.
Young LGBTQ people with at least one accepting adult report better mental health (Trevor Project, a US study).
Trans and non-binary young people report more bullying and exclusion at school (Trevor Project).
School routines such as sports teams, toilets and trips are often split into two groups.
